To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there exist a variety of OWA operators that can be used for modeling the utility adjustment process, (2) our model is closely related to proportional representation voting models, and (3) depending on the OWA operators, our model is NP-hard but admits good approximation algorithms.

(i) we introduce the model of collective item selection that is applicable in many practical scenarios; (ii) the problem is NP-hard; (iii) there exist good approximation algorithms for some special cases.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding the most desirable set of items for a group of agents, given that each agent derives a fraction of his or her intrinsic utility for an item depending on the item’s rank.
a new type of group recommendation problem where the goal is to maximize the derived utility of all agents.
the problem of group decision making in a setting where agents’ preferences are not fully revealed, but rather only their relative rankings are known.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general framework for modeling group decision making and provide efficient approximation algorithms for the resulting optimization problem.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in many practical settings, the OWA model provides a good and simple approximation of the underlying process of utility adjustment.
, when the agents’ utilities are adjusted in a certain manner (i.e., using OWA operators), we can efficiently find good solutions to our problem.
OWA-based models can be used for a wide variety of problems, and in particular for group recommendation problems.
